sentences.text: This animal was a medium-sized, four-legged plant eater that moved on the ground.
It could reach a length of 5 meters and a mass of 2 tonnes.
Its head featured a short, curved horn on the nose, no horns above the eyes, and a short neck shield with forward-pointing spikes that looked like a crown.
The skull measured 180 centimeters long, making it one of the biggest known for this specific group of horned dinosaurs.
A distinct line of small bumps ran along the top of the neck shield, a feature never seen in other horned dinosaurs.
This species was the very first horned dinosaur discovered in China and remains the only one known from the entire Asian continent.
Its discovery was significant because it proved that these large, horned creatures existed in Asia.
Scientists named this genus in 2010 after finding three skulls in Zhucheng, China.
The main specimen, which includes a partial skull with the brain case, was found during the summer of 2008.
Paleontologist Xu Xing and his team officially described and named the new genus that year.
The name translates to "Chinese horned face," combining Latin and Greek words for China, horn, and face.

It shared its environment with the common duck-billed dinosaur Shantungosaurus, the tyrannosaur Zhuchengtyrannus, the small horned dinosaur Zhuchengceratops, and the large duck-billed dinosaur Huaxiaosaurus.
This animal belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
It is classified within the subfamily Centrosaurinae.
Researchers placed it as a basal member of this subfamily based on the shape of its skull.
This creature lived between 77.3 and 73.5 million years ago in what is now Shandong province, China.
It lived alongside Shantungosaurus, Zhuchengtyrannus, Zhuchengceratops, and Huaxiaosaurus in the same geological layer.
It is debated whether this species represents a lineage that moved from North America into Asia, given that it shares traits with advanced forms not found in primitive ones.
